Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

to preposition

towards a place or a person: go to, come to

classical

Ter. Ad. 970: ehō, accēde hūc ad mē
Cic. Fam. 9.4.1: tū sī minus ad nōs, nōs accurrēmus ad tē

ad (+ accusative)

preposition with the accusative

to, up to (a place or a person)

Ad takes you to a place or a person, up to it or into its presence; in with the accusative takes you into it (see into). Ad forum īre, go to the forum; ad mē venī, come to me, and so to my house (see at the house of). Giving or saying something to someone is the dative, with no preposition: dā mihi.

Other words

  • domum, rūs; Rōmam (accusative alone) — home, to the country; to Rome

    accusative without a preposition · classical · Ter. Ad. 699: Abī domum; Verg. E. 10.77: īte domum saturae

    Names of towns and small islands, domus and rūs take no preposition: Rōmam proficīscī, domum redīre. Ad with a town’s name is to its neighbourhood, up to it: ad Capuam.

  • in (+ accusative) — to (a country, a region)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Vulg. Gen. 28.15: redūcam tē in terram hanc

    Of a country or a region Latin goes “into” it: in Graeciam proficīscī, go to Greece.

Examples

  • ehō, accēde hūc ad mē

    here, come over to meTer. Ad. 970

  • ego eō ad forum, nisi quid vīs

    I’m off to the forum, unless you want somethingPlaut. Asin. 108

  • tū sī minus ad nōs, nōs accurrēmus ad tē

    if you don’t come to us, we will hurry to youCic. Fam. 9.4.1

  • Abī domum, ac deōs comprecāre ut uxōrem arcessās: abī.

    Go home and pray to the gods, so that you can fetch your bride: go!Ter. Ad. 699

  • īte domum saturae, venit Hesperus, īte capellae

    go home, my well-fed goats, the evening star is coming, goVerg. E. 10.77

  • Et erō custōs tuus quōcumque perrēxeris, et redūcam tē in terram hanc

    And I will keep you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this landVulg. Gen. 28.15

See also into, towards, from, at the house of, house.
